purpose: Independent forward use of the current Skill for nondefault sealed pilot controls and complete-inventory obligations.

model.selection: inherited Codex session default; fresh agent without parent history
model.limitation: Exact model build and sampling seed were not exposed.

observed_scope: One fresh agent handled two read-only scenarios; no pilot, gate or test execution was requested or claimed.

assessment.method: Post-run qualitative review of retained actions and answers; no desired answers were supplied to the agent.
assessment.pilot: Preserved the sealed 1+1 inventory and limit 3; two nonprogress attempts alone do not require stopping. Identified blocker-set and report-binding evidence gaps.
assessment.file_contract: Identified that change: all/full does not establish every historical per-file obligation; routed to an adequate existing complete-inventory check or an explicit gap.

limitations: Single observations are not a reliability benchmark.
The pilot excerpt is not an authenticated manifest or trial outcome.
No real project was supplied for the inventory scenario.
Legacy runtime and existing-package migration choices were not exercised here.

artifacts.text:
1	---
     2	name: qualitygate-cli
     3	description: "Verify implementation, bug-fix and refactor changes with Qualitygate CLI, author source-bound repository rules, and review design contracts with evidence. Also use for rule configuration, runtime verification and selfcheck."
     4	metadata:
     5	  version: "1.2.0"
     6	  homepage: "https://github.com/coolplayagent/qualitygate-cli"
     7	---
     8	
     9	# Qualitygate CLI
    10	
    11	Use this Skill to select the appropriate evidence and workflow; use the matching
    12	`qualitygate` executable for Schema export, source binding, validation, generation,
    13	planning and checks. An agent's interpretation never replaces a CLI result.
    14	Preserve the user's scope, selected runtime and existing authorization.
    15	
    16	## Choose the task before running commands
    17	
    18	| Task | Read when applicable | Boundary |
    19	| --- | --- | --- |
    20	| Verify implementation, bug fixes or refactors | [Verification](references/verification.md) | Establish the selected policy, run the final full check and retain its evidence. |
    21	| Inspect help, capabilities or schemas; verify the runtime | [Runtime startup](references/runtime-startup.md), [compatibility](references/runtime-compatibility.md), [selfcheck](references/selfcheck.md) | These operations need no repository policy; do not initialize one for them. |
    22	| Discover or configure rules | [Rule management](references/rule-management.md), [bundled rules](references/builtin-rules.md) | Read-only discovery can precede initialization; policy context requires the selected existing policy. Candidate edits need authorization within the current task. |
    23	| Translate explicit repository constraints into rules | [Rule authoring](references/rule-authoring.md) | Select V1/V2/V3 by supported evidence, export the matching Schema, bind sources and validate before generation. Generation is not adoption. |
    24	| Review responsibility, dependencies, duplicated knowledge or interface behavior | [Design review](references/design-review.md) | Apply Clean Code, Clean Architecture, DRY and SOLID to concrete contracts and counterexamples. Contextual review is not a deterministic gate. |
    25	| Review concurrency, lifetime, bounds, cross-path behavior or tests | [Public review pack](references/review-pack.md) | Select the relevant cards and retain evidence gaps; do not infer safety from text patterns. |
    26	
    27	Read only the references needed for the task. Runtime inspection, rule discovery
    28	and review-only requests do not imply a full repository check or policy adoption.
    29	For code changes, the verification workflow remains a prerequisite to completion.
    30	
    31	## Execution and authority invariants
    32	
    33	Use the existing repository policy and applicable task contract. Never weaken a
    34	required check, fabricate an approval, invent a trusted ref, or suppress a missing
    35	capability to produce a pass. Separately required repository checks still apply.
    36	Resolve findings within the authorized task and recheck after input changes.
    37	
    38	Code-task completion requires the final unfiltered `profile: full` report with
    39	`scope: delivery` or `scope: task`, empty `plan.pending_delivery_checks`,
    40	`gate.complete: true`, `gate.decision: pass` and exit code `0`, plus separately
    41	required checks. Quick/path feedback, preflight, schema validity, prompt delivery
    42	and warning triage each provide narrower evidence. Preserve warnings, incomplete
    43	execution and unknowns. Follow [verification](references/verification.md) for the
    44	complete decision and initialization procedure.
    45	
    46	When reporting `check` or `selfcheck`, preserve `verification.conclusion`,
    47	`verified_shapes`, `known_limits` and `unverified_assumptions`. A pass concerns
    48	the verified shapes and scope; it is not proof of a defect-free deployment.
    49	
    50	For rule authoring, the LLM may draft a candidate but must use the matching CLI's
    51	source and validation results. Read the complete exported Schema and keep
    52	unsupported obligations explicit. Do not extend the finite DSL from memory or
    53	describe a review signal as proof of a semantic defect. Existing authorization
    54	can cover candidate edits; approval and adoption remain separate decisions.
    55	
    56	When effective policy declares `agent_obligations`, obtain the current
    57	`agent-contract` projection with the selected role, task and policy before acting.
    58	Apply its prompt to the consuming agent and reload after resume, handoff or
    59	relevant input changes. Read [Agent contracts](references/agent-contracts.md).
    60	Required gaps block readiness; a ready projection proves neither compliance nor
    61	host enforcement. Preserve higher-priority instructions and existing permissions.
    62	Required host controls need an actual supporting host, not an acknowledgement.
    63	
    64	## Runtime and path conventions
    65	
    66	Resolve the installed Skill and target repository independently:
    67	
    68	| Input | Owner and path |
    69	| --- | --- |
    70	| `QUALITYGATE_SKILL_ROOT` | Absolute installation directory containing this `SKILL.md` |
    71	| `QUALITYGATE_BIN` | Explicitly selected trusted executable, otherwise the matching `assets/<platform>-<architecture>/qualitygate[.exe]` or verified published PATH runtime |
    72	| Built-in assets | Installation's `references/rules/`; optional explicit `QUALITYGATE_BUILTIN_RULES_DIR` |
    73	| Schemas | Installation's `references/schemas/`, compared with runtime exports |
    74	| `REPOSITORY_ROOT` | Absolute root of the target repository, when needed |
    75	| `QUALITYGATE_CONFIG` | `qualitygate.yaml`, or the caller's normalized repository-relative `--config` path |
    76	| Project candidates | Repository's `qualitygate/rules/`; discovery honors legacy `custom_rules` |
    77	| Policy history | Repository's `.qualitygate/policy/` |
    78	
    79	Use the shell-specific [startup examples](references/runtime-startup.md). Preserve
    80	an explicit executable or asset override and report invalid selections; do not
    81	silently replace them. Choose assets for the actual OS and architecture. Do not
    82	build an untrusted checkout as the runtime. Version equality does not establish
    83	build identity: inspect capabilities, executable digest and matching assets.
    84	
    85	Carry the same `--root`, `--config` and selected policy/task inputs through relevant
    86	commands. Reference examples without `--config` assume the default. Bind variables
    87	again across isolated tool calls. `skill:references/rules/...` is provenance, not
    88	a repository-relative path. Built-in YAML is runtime data; project configuration
    89	is the candidate-edit surface. Discovery does not enable enforcement.
    90	
    91	## Initialization prerequisite
    92	
    93	For repository verification, follow the canonical
    94	[configuration prerequisite](references/verification.md#initialization-prerequisite).
    95	Identify the selected policy authority first. A confirmed missing local candidate
    96	requires ordinary automatic `init` when no active policy or explicit policy ref
    97	is selected. Missing or invalid selected refs and signed policies require their
    98	own diagnosis; local initialization cannot repair them. Keep discovery and
    99	runtime-only tasks outside this prerequisite. Initialization does not authorize
   100	command adoption, rule enabling or policy adoption.
   101	
   102	## Additional workflows
   103	
   104	| Need | Reference and control surface |
   105	| --- | --- |
   106	| Select snapshots, trim acquisition inputs or preserve trust evidence | [Operations](references/operations.md); snapshot selectors, reviewed exclusions and external evidence |
   107	| Bound instruction size or retain required paths | [File contracts](references/file-contracts.md); `file` with `change: all` |
   108	| Require assertion counterexamples against old code | [Test effectiveness](references/test-effectiveness.md); explicit command/task `test_effectiveness` |
   109	| Prevent analyzer debt growth | [Diagnostic ratchets](references/diagnostic-ratchets.md); report `mode: ratchet` with a fresh base run |
   110	| Compose typed predicates and bounded counts | [V2 operators](references/operators.md); `rules.operators.v2` |
   111	| Relate collections with lexical lambdas and projections | [V3 operators](references/operators-v3.md); `rules.operators.v3` |
   112	| Track declared clauses, adoption, unsupported gaps and snapshot execution | [Constraint coverage](references/constraint-coverage.md); `schema constraint`, automatic `constraint-coverage` check |
   113	| Run the selected Rust Agent host with guarded delivery | [Agent host](references/agent-host.md); `agent-run`, injection receipts, fresh full checks and immutable export |
   114	| Supply bounded repair context | [Agent feedback](references/agent-feedback.md); `check --feedback` and full rechecks |
   115	| Consume versioned decisions or assess warnings | [Decision protocol](references/decision-protocol.md); schemas, optional `--envelope` and advisory judgment |
   116	| Seal or independently accept a declared pilot inventory | [Pilot evidence](references/pilot-evidence.md); signed owner/reviewer records and full-report bindings |
   117	
   118	File contracts and diagnostic ratchets are not additional built-in IDs for
   119	`rules enable`. The CLI advertises actual rule definitions and parameter contracts
   120	through `rules list` and `rules describe`; use that inventory rather than treating
   121	this Skill's examples as exhaustive. A missing capability is a compatibility gap.
   122	Neither a prompt's design recommendation nor an enabled pattern signal proves
   123	that a repository satisfies Clean Architecture or SOLID.

artifacts.text:
1	# Pilot evidence summaries
     2	
     3	For a new pilot, the bundled
     4	[v10 manifest template](../assets/pilot/observation-v10.json) provides an example.
     5	Complete the caller-selected protocol and assignment matrix, then run
     6	`qualitygate pilot seal --input <plan.json>
     7	--format json` before collecting outcomes. Retain that stdout as the observation
     8	manifest in the declared external archive. Sealing rejects existing observations,
     9	incomplete governance, non-real inputs, missing ground truth and unbalanced
    10	model/workflow cohorts. Preserve the selected inventory, task mix and retry
    11	limits; an already sealed protocol must retain its exact declared values.
    12	
    13	Manifest schema v3 and later require a predeclared `protocol.task_mix`. The
    14	bundled example uses four independent `bug_fix` and four independent `refactor`
    15	inputs. The selected counts must sum to `task_count` and match distinct input IDs
    16	in the assignment matrix. Distinct inputs cannot reuse a task ID or task-contract
    17	digest. The summary's `sampling_audit` lists the declared and observed counts and one task
    18	identity per input. Review real issue/commit sources and sampling records before
    19	sealing; distinct strings and digests cannot prove semantic independence.
    20	
    21	Manifest schema v4 also requires one `sources` entry for each independent input.
    22	Declare an issue or commit source ID, the archive-relative path, exact byte
    23	length, SHA-256 digest and selection time no later than sealing. Keep each
    24	regular source file beside the external observation manifest (at most 64 KiB
    25	each and 8 MiB total). The CLI checks confined paths and bytes at seal, start
    26	subject, summary and final subject calls; missing or changed files are incomplete
    27	evidence. `source_audit` shows one source per input. Human reviewers must still
    28	confirm that the files match real, distinct issue/commit records and that the
    29	selection time is credible.
    30	
    31	Manifest schema v5 also requires `run_order`: every assignment ID exactly once,
    32	adjacent workflows alternating, with existing-tools-first and qualitygate-first
    33	counts balanced within each task-kind and requested-model stratum. Record each
    34	actual run's `start_sequence` (1-based) in its observation. The summary's
    35	`schedule_audit` reports missing positions and deviations; either blocks final
    36	acceptance. Do not infer start order from completion timestamps. Compare the
    37	declared positions with retained external start-event logs.
    38	
    39	Manifest schema v6 additionally requires a digest-bound initial full report for
    40	every assignment and a sealed `protocol.no_progress_limit` between 1 and
    41	`max_attempts`, inclusive. The bundled example uses 2.
    42	The CLI verifies each baseline report against the initial snapshot, task,
    43	policy, environment, tools and required checks, then rereads its archived bytes
    44	for seal, start subject, summary and final subject calls. Initial and attempt
    45	reports share a 64 MiB read budget. `attempt_audit` recomputes progress only
    46	when the set of error diagnostic identities and gate blockers strictly shrinks
    47	in a complete bound full report. Failed, timed-out or abandoned attempts with
    48	no report count as no verified progress. Runs that exceed the sealed attempt/time
    49	cap or continue after reaching the sealed no-progress limit block final acceptance
    50	while remaining in cost and failure denominators. Review external Agent/clock logs
    51	to establish the truth of declared durations and outcomes.
    52	
    53	For older sealed v7 records, `model_evidence` belongs to each observation. Archive one JSON
    54	capture per run and declare its confined relative path, SHA-256 and byte length
    55	alongside the same structured capture in the manifest. Bind assignment ID,
    56	Agent version, harness digest, requested model, reasoning effort and capture
    57	time. Use `status: unknown`, `actual_model: null` and a nonempty
    58	`unknown_reason` when the provider does not expose a routed model. Use
    59	`status: reported` with `actual_model` and no unknown reason only when an
    60	actual model is reported. The capture must match the assignment's post-run
    61	`cohort.actual_model`; the requested fields must match the sealed plan. Missing
    62	captures make evidence incomplete. An explicit unknown actual model does not
    63	block v7 protocol readiness; comparisons are about requested configurations.
    64	Review the provider's original logs and clock independently: an archived
    65	capture is a declaration, not authenticated provider routing.
    66	
    67	For an unknown routed model, write the `capture` object below as a JSON file
    68	in the external pilot archive. Put its exact relative path, SHA-256 and byte
    69	length in `model_evidence.artifact`, and put the same parsed object in
    70	`model_evidence.capture`:
    71	
    72	```json
    73	{
    74	  "assignment_id": "run-01",
    75	  "captured_at": 1780000000,
    76	  "agent_version": "recorded-agent-version",
    77	  "harness_digest": "sha256:replace-with-real-digest",
    78	  "requested_model": "requested-model",
    79	  "reasoning_effort": "medium",
    80	  "actual_model": null,
    81	  "status": "unknown",
    82	  "unknown_reason": "Provider response did not expose a routed model identifier"
    83	}
    84	```
    85	
    86	The example values are placeholders, not valid trial evidence. Capture time
    87	must be within the sealed window and no later than `observed_at`. The CLI
    88	limits each model file to 64 KiB and the model inventory to 8 MiB. For a
    89	reported model, set `status` to `reported`, use the provider's model string in
    90	`actual_model`, and set `unknown_reason` to null. A reviewer still needs the
    91	provider's original record to assess that claim.
    92	
    93	Manifest schema v8 moves model evidence to each attempt. Keep
    94	`observation.model_evidence` absent. For every recorded attempt, including a
    95	failed, timed-out or abandoned one, add `attempt.model_evidence` with the same
    96	`artifact` and `capture` shape. The capture JSON adds `attempt_number`, equal to
    97	the containing attempt's `number`; archive each JSON file separately. For
    98	example, an unknown model on attempt 2 uses:
    99	
   100	```json
   101	{
   102	  "assignment_id": "run-01",
   103	  "attempt_number": 2,
   104	  "captured_at": 1780000000,
   105	  "agent_version": "recorded-agent-version",
   106	  "harness_digest": "sha256:replace-with-real-digest",
   107	  "requested_model": "requested-model",
   108	  "reasoning_effort": "medium",
   109	  "actual_model": null,
   110	  "status": "unknown",
   111	  "unknown_reason": "Provider response did not expose a routed model identifier"
   112	}
   113	```
   114	
   115	Missing attempt captures make the result incomplete, even if a later attempt
   116	passes. If all captures report the same actual model, set the assignment's
   117	`cohort.actual_model` to that value. Otherwise leave it null. Two different
   118	reported actual models within one assigned run are a protocol deviation and
   119	block final acceptance. An unknown model is an explicit data state, not a
   120	claim that two reported routes match. `model_audit` lists every attempt,
   121	including failed and timed-out ones, plus missing captures and drifted runs.
   122	The 64 KiB per-file and 8 MiB total limits still apply. The archived claim,
   123	capture time and provider routing remain subject to independent review.
   124	
   125	Manifest schema v9 also requires an archived execution receipt for each
   126	recorded attempt. Put `execution_evidence` beside `model_evidence`, with an
   127	`artifact` containing a confined relative path, exact byte length and SHA-256
   128	and a `capture` matching the strict JSON file. A failed or timed-out attempt
   129	still needs its own receipt. For example:
   130	
   131	```json
   132	{
   133	  "assignment_id": "run-01",
   134	  "attempt_number": 2,
   135	  "started_at_ms": 1780000000000,
   136	  "ended_at_ms": 1780000001000,
   137	  "harness_digest": "sha256:replace-with-real-digest",
   138	  "status": "timed_out",
   139	  "snapshot_digest": "sha256:replace-with-real-digest",
   140	  "report_digest": null
   141	}
   142	```
   143	
   144	The start and end are Unix milliseconds. Their difference must equal the
   145	attempt's `elapsed_ms`, and the receipt must match the assignment, attempt
   146	number, sealed harness, status, snapshot and optional report digest. Times
   147	must fall inside the sealed window and end no later than `observed_at`;
   148	recorded attempts in one run cannot overlap. The `execution_audit` lists
   149	missing receipts and compares the first archived start in each run to its
   150	declared `start_sequence`. Equal or reversed starts block final acceptance.
   151	Missing receipts make the result incomplete. Each strict JSON file is limited
   152	to 64 KiB and the receipt inventory to 8 MiB. The CLI rereads the files for
   153	each output; the independent reviewer must compare them with original
   154	process and clock logs. The digest does not authenticate execution or time.
   155	
   156	Manifest schemas v2-v9 require a structured `protocol.budget`: three-letter
   157	uppercase currency, price timestamp, rate-card source, total cap in currency
   158	microunits, and human hourly rate in microunits. Set legacy `monetary_cap` to
   159	null. The cap covers all model and infrastructure attempts in both workflows,
   160	including failed attempts, plus each observation's active human review time.
   161	Missing costs, time, or incompatible currency/price are unknown; known spend
   162	above the cap fails even if other inputs are unknown. Budget fields are sealed
   163	before observation. Already sealed v1 records retain their original nine-check
   164	assessment and human interpretation of the text cap.
   165	
   166	For new v10 plans, set `monetary_cap` to null, leave `budget` null or absent,
   167	and leave `thresholds.cost_ratio_max` null or absent. The bundled template omits
   168	the threshold. The signed assessment uses eight nonfinancial
   169	checks: detection, false positives, repair, required-check completion, review
   170	fraction, matched inventory, review-time reduction and full-P95 duration.
   171	Costs and usage may still be recorded as descriptive observations; missing
   172	prices remain unknown and do not block those eight checks. v1-v9 plans keep
   173	their versioned financial requirements and assessment digests.
   174	
   175	Before collecting outcomes, run `qualitygate pilot authorization-subject
   176	--input <observations.json> --format json`. Have the configured human owner sign
   177	the exact subject as a DSSE Ed25519 record with payload type
   178	`application/vnd.qualitygate.pilot-plan-authorization.v1+json`. The trust key ID
   179	must equal the protocol owner and allow repository checks with the
   180	`pilot-plan-authorization` scope. Keep the trust store and signed envelope
   181	outside the checked repository; do not ask the CLI or an Agent to create a key.
   182	
   183	Use `qualitygate pilot summarize --input <observations.json> --trust-store
   184	<external-trust.json> --authorization <external-start.dsse.json> --format json`
   185	for authenticated aggregation. Omitting both external inputs remains a read-only
   186	descriptive replay with `plan_authorization.status=absent` and
   187	`protocol_ready=false`. Keep report paths relative to the manifest's external archive.
   188	
   189	The command verifies report bytes and their task, policy, snapshot, environment,
   190	tool and required-check bindings. It retains missing, failed, timed-out and
   191	abandoned assignments in denominators. Null metrics mean that evidence or a
   192	denominator is missing; do not replace them with zero. Different model,
   193	permission, tool, environment, cache, origin, task type and workflow declarations
   194	remain separate groups.
   195	
   196	The embedded plan digest detects later changes to the protocol and assignments;
   197	actual routed model identities and observations may be added after sealing.
   198	The owner signature authenticates that exact subject and is checked for scope,
   199	validity and revocation on each summary; it is not a trusted timestamp or final
   200	trial acceptance. The output is descriptive. Reviewer identities, canonical
   201	issue truth, any supplied prices and authority are caller declarations. Do not treat a
   202	summary or met threshold as signed trial approval, and do not infer causal
   203	benefit from groups without the same declared input inventory and conditions.
   204	
   205	After the observation window, use `pilot acceptance-subject` with the same
   206	external trust store and authenticated start record. Review the five candidate
   207	rates (detection, false-positive, repair, completion and review fraction) plus
   208	matched inventory, review-time reduction and full-P95 duration. v1-v9 also
   209	require the cost comparison; v2-v9 additionally require the total-budget check.
   210	v10 requires only the eight nonfinancial checks. Failed or unknown required
   211	checks cannot be signed as accepted.
   212	
   213	The independent human reviewer key must equal the protocol reviewer and have
   214	the `pilot-trial-acceptance` repository scope. Sign the exact subject with
   215	payload type `application/vnd.qualitygate.pilot-trial-acceptance.v1+json`, then
   216	pass the external envelope with `pilot summarize --acceptance`. An authenticated
   217	rejection is a blocking result. A signature authenticates the decision over the
   218	retained evidence; it does not establish causal benefit or authorize automatic
   219	rollout. Older sealed manifests keep their versioned validation and acceptance
   220	semantics; use this bundled reference for a new v10 pilot.

artifacts.text:
1	# Instruction budgets and required files
     2	
     3	Use this workflow for instruction inventory totals, changed-file budgets or
     4	deletion of explicitly named owner/test files. It uses the
     5	project-rule DSL and `files` capability, without adding a command or built-in
     6	rule ID. Read [rule authoring](rule-authoring.md) for source binding, schema
     7	compatibility, candidate generation and adoption.
     8	
     9	## Author the requested contract
    10	
    11	The CLI selects per-file findings only for changed files in the chosen snapshot.
    12	A delivery pass does not establish that unchanged files meet per-file contracts
    13	or that every required path exists. A path absent from both base and current
    14	snapshots has no selected deletion, so its missing-path finding is filtered.
    15	Unlocated inventory totals (`min_count`, `max_count`, `max_total_words`) remain
    16	aggregate constraints over the configured unexcluded inventory; a changed-line
    17	filter cannot establish those totals from changed files alone. Policy `exclude`
    18	removes resources before acquisition, so required build inputs must be retained.
    19	
    20	If the requested obligation covers every file or required path regardless of
    21	Git changes, these per-file assertions alone do not satisfy it. Use the
    22	repository's existing complete-inventory command check when it proves that
    23	obligation, or retain an unsupported evidence gap. Configuring a new check
    24	requires authorization within the task; do not silently reduce the obligation
    25	to changed files or invent a CLI repository-scope option.
    26	
    27	Inspect `rules list --source project --format json` and the actual normative
    28	section first. Take paths, budgets and severity from that requirement. The
    29	following candidate illustrates the fields; replace its source block with the
    30	exact result of `rules source` and adapt its assertions to the reviewed policy:
    31	
    32	```yaml
    33	id: instruction-inventory
    34	schema_version: 1
    35	version: 1
    36	source:
    37	  document: AGENTS.md
    38	  section: Instruction maintenance
    39	  content_hash: 'sha256:<exact section digest from rules source>'
    40	requires_capabilities: [files]
    41	applies_to:
    42	  paths: [AGENTS.md, AGENTS.project.md, CLAUDE.md]
    43	when: {entity: file, change: all}
    44	then:
    45	  min_count: 3
    46	  max_lines: 300
    47	  max_total_words: 4000
    48	  required_paths: [src/net/client.rs, tests/network_contract.rs]
    49	fix: Keep instructions within the reviewed budget and restore required owner or test files
    50	```
    51	
    52	| Assertion | Meaning |
    53	|---|---|
    54	| `min_count` / `max_count` | Minimum / maximum number of matching files; `min_count` can fail on zero matches |
    55	| `max_lines` | Per-file text lines; LF/CRLF delimit lines, a final newline adds no empty line, empty files have zero lines |
    56	| `max_total_words` | Combined Unicode whitespace-separated segments in matching UTF-8 files, including code and comments |
    57	| `required_paths` | Look up up to 256 unique normalized literal repository-relative files in the captured snapshot; missing-path findings follow delivery and feedback selection |
    58	
    59	`max_lines`, `max_total_words` and `required_paths` require
    60	`when: {entity: file, change: all}`. Zero is a valid numeric limit;
    61	`min_count` cannot exceed `max_count`. Omitted `change` means `added`, while
    62	`any` remains limited to changed files and cannot enforce these assertions.
    63	
    64	Text inventory respects `applies_to` language/path filters and CLI `--path`.
    65	Required-path lookup uses the complete captured snapshot even outside those
    66	filters or with no matching text. Its located findings still require a selected
    67	changed path and can be filtered by CLI `--path`; lookup is not a repository-wide
    68	existence gate. Required paths are files, not directories, symbols or globs;
    69	the snapshot rejects symlinks. Scope this rule to intended
    70	text files: invalid UTF-8 is incomplete execution. Selection and measurement
    71	each have a 30-second deadline, with at most 50,000 files and 32 MiB selected
    72	text; snapshot budgets apply independently.
    73	
    74	Validate and generate through the [authoring sequence](rule-authoring.md#extraction-sequence).
    75	Generation does not enable the rule. Adoption needs the selected project-rule
    76	directory, enabled ID/profiles and the repository's bound source review.
    77	Missing/stale review remains incomplete; a newly computed hash cannot replace
    78	review. Do not edit the installed built-in rule assets to add a project rule.
    79	
    80	## Check, repair and recheck
    81	
    82	Run the caller's selector/profile using [operations](operations.md). Inspect
    83	the rule's `metadata.file_inventory`: `files`, `lines`, `words`, `word_unit`,
    84	`required_paths` and `snapshot_digest`. Use each diagnostic's assertion,
    85	evidence, fix and pinned recheck to locate excess text or a missing file.
    86	
    87	Repair the requested content while preserving its obligations, or restore the
    88	actual required implementation/test. Do not create an empty file solely to
    89	satisfy presence or raise budgets to make a failure pass. A staged check still
    90	reads index bytes after a worktree repair; retain the requested selector and
    91	report when the repair has not been staged. Recheck the same policy and scope;
    92	path-scoped or quick feedback does not establish full delivery readiness.
    93	
    94	Retain failures and incomplete evidence separately. Whitespace segments are
    95	neither model tokens nor linguistic words. File presence does not prove
    96	ownership, agent compliance or test effectiveness. Behavioral obligations need
    97	the project's actual tests, rule evidence and review.
    98	
    99	## Required text and nonempty scans
   100	
   101	`then.require_pattern` requires a Rust regex match in every triggered entity's
   102	text. Pair it with `then.min_count` when an empty scan must fail. The minimum
   103	supports all valid entity/change combinations and counts triggered entities;
   104	retained marker obligations do not satisfy it. Source bindings, review records
   105	and explicit adoption still apply. Missing capabilities and failed parsing are
   106	incomplete, not zero matches. For a reviewed contract-field rule, prove the
   107	missing-text and empty-inventory failures separately before adoption.

1	# Resolve the runtime
     2	
     3	Read only the example for the active OS and shell. Set the Skill root to the
     4	absolute directory containing `SKILL.md`, `references/` and, in a complete
     5	release archive, `assets/`. Runtime selection needs no repository or policy.
     6	
     7	Preserve an explicitly selected `QUALITYGATE_BIN` (Bash) or `$QualitygateBin`
     8	(PowerShell). It must identify the authorized absolute executable path; an
     9	invalid explicit selection is an error, not permission to switch builds.
    10	Otherwise prefer the matching bundled asset, then an already verified
    11	published executable on PATH when that asset is missing or unusable. A user
    12	may explicitly select a verified development build for authorized CLI work;
    13	identify it as a development build rather than a published release.
    14	
    15	Establish the selected binary's provenance before running these examples.
    16	PATH lookup, `--version`, a capabilities response and a self-reported digest
    17	do not authenticate a binary. Do not build a repository checkout, install a
    18	runtime or replace an installed copy merely to make startup succeed.
    19	
    20	Record the executable and rule-asset bindings and reapply them in each fresh
    21	tool shell. Complete archives discover their own assets. An explicit or PATH
    22	runtime uses this matching Skill's assets when no override was supplied.
    23	Preserve an existing `QUALITYGATE_BUILTIN_RULES_DIR`; it names the directory
    24	containing `core/`, `shared/` and language packages. An invalid explicit override
    25	is an error, not a reason to select different assets. A directory's existence
    26	does not prove its compatibility with the binary.
    27	
    28	The examples below require a runtime advertising `capabilities` in its help;
    29	they query `--version` and capabilities only. Compare their results using
    30	[runtime compatibility](runtime-compatibility.md). For an explicitly selected
    31	older runtime without that command, use the separate
    32	[legacy inspection](runtime-compatibility.md#legacy-runtime-inspection) first,
    33	not these scripts. A capabilities execution failure is a runtime error, not
    34	evidence that the binary is old or permission to install a replacement.
    35	
    36	## Linux and WSL: Bash
    37	
    38	Set `QUALITYGATE_SKILL_ROOT`. Optionally set `QUALITYGATE_BIN` to the explicitly
    39	selected executable. Linux and WSL use Linux assets; macOS has no bundled asset
    40	and uses an authorized explicit executable or verified PATH runtime.
    41	
    42	```bash
    43	: "${QUALITYGATE_SKILL_ROOT:?Set the absolute Skill directory}"
    44	qualitygate_external_runtime=false
    45	if [ "${QUALITYGATE_BIN+x}" = x ]; then
    46	  test -n "$QUALITYGATE_BIN" && test -x "$QUALITYGATE_BIN" || { echo "Invalid explicit Qualitygate executable" >&2; exit 2; }
    47	  "$QUALITYGATE_BIN" --version || exit 2
    48	  qualitygate_external_runtime=true
    49	else
    50	  qualitygate_asset=""
    51	  if [ "$(uname -s)" = Linux ]; then
    52	    case "$(uname -m)" in
    53	      x86_64|amd64) qualitygate_asset=linux-x86_64 ;;
    54	      aarch64|arm64) qualitygate_asset=linux-aarch64 ;;
    55	    esac
    56	  fi
    57	  QUALITYGATE_BIN="$QUALITYGATE_SKILL_ROOT/assets/$qualitygate_asset/qualitygate"
    58	  if [ -z "$qualitygate_asset" ] || ! test -x "$QUALITYGATE_BIN" || ! "$QUALITYGATE_BIN" --version; then
    59	    QUALITYGATE_BIN="$(command -v qualitygate)" || exit 2
    60	    "$QUALITYGATE_BIN" --version || exit 2
    61	    qualitygate_external_runtime=true
    62	  fi
    63	fi
    64	if [ "$qualitygate_external_runtime" = true ] && [ "${QUALITYGATE_BUILTIN_RULES_DIR+x}" != x ]; then
    65	  QUALITYGATE_BUILTIN_RULES_DIR="$QUALITYGATE_SKILL_ROOT/references/rules"
    66	fi
    67	if [ "${QUALITYGATE_BUILTIN_RULES_DIR+x}" = x ]; then
    68	  test -d "$QUALITYGATE_BUILTIN_RULES_DIR" || { echo "Invalid Qualitygate rule asset directory" >&2; exit 2; }
    69	  export QUALITYGATE_BUILTIN_RULES_DIR
    70	fi
    71	"$QUALITYGATE_BIN" capabilities --format json || exit 2
    72	```
    73	
    74	## Windows: PowerShell
    75	
    76	Set `$QualitygateSkillRoot` to a native absolute path. Optionally set
    77	`$QualitygateBin` to the explicitly selected executable's native absolute path.
    78	
    79	```powershell
    80	if (-not $QualitygateSkillRoot) { throw "Set the absolute Skill directory" }
    81	$qualitygateExternalRuntime = $false
    82	if ($null -ne $QualitygateBin) {
    83	  if (-not $QualitygateBin -or -not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $QualitygateBin -PathType Leaf)) {
    84	    throw "Invalid explicit Qualitygate executable"
    85	  }
    86	  & $QualitygateBin --version
    87	  if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "Explicit Qualitygate runtime is unusable" }
    88	  $qualitygateExternalRuntime = $true
    89	} else {
    90	  $architecture = [System.Runtime.InteropServices.RuntimeInformation]::OSArchitecture.ToString()
    91	  $assetDirectory = if ([System.Runtime.InteropServices.RuntimeInformation]::IsOSPlatform([System.Runtime.InteropServices.OSPlatform]::Windows)) {
    92	    if ($architecture -eq "X64") { "windows-x86_64" }
    93	    elseif ($architecture -eq "Arm64") { "windows-aarch64" }
    94	  } else { $null }
    95	  $QualitygateBin = if ($assetDirectory) {
    96	    Join-Path $QualitygateSkillRoot "assets/$assetDirectory/qualitygate.exe"
    97	  } else { $null }
    98	  $qualitygateReady = $false
    99	  if ($QualitygateBin -and (Test-Path -LiteralPath $QualitygateBin -PathType Leaf)) {
   100	    try {
   101	      & $QualitygateBin --version
   102	      $qualitygateReady = $LASTEXITCODE -eq 0
   103	    } catch { $qualitygateReady = $false }
   104	  }
   105	  if (-not $qualitygateReady) {
   106	    $QualitygateBin = (Get-Command qualitygate -CommandType Application -ErrorAction Stop | Select-Object -First 1).Source
   107	    & $QualitygateBin --version
   108	    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "Qualitygate runtime is unusable" }
   109	    $qualitygateExternalRuntime = $true
   110	  }
   111	}
   112	if ($qualitygateExternalRuntime -and -not (Test-Path Env:QUALITYGATE_BUILTIN_RULES_DIR)) {
   113	  $env:QUALITYGATE_BUILTIN_RULES_DIR = Join-Path $QualitygateSkillRoot "references/rules"
   114	}
   115	if (Test-Path Env:QUALITYGATE_BUILTIN_RULES_DIR) {
   116	  if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $env:QUALITYGATE_BUILTIN_RULES_DIR -PathType Container)) {
   117	    throw "Invalid Qualitygate rule asset directory"
   118	  }
   119	}
   120	& $QualitygateBin capabilities --format json
   121	if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "Qualitygate capabilities are unavailable" }
   122	```
   123	
   124	## Windows: native Git Bash/MSYS2
   125	
   126	Native Windows `.exe` files work in Git Bash/MSYS2. Supply shell paths for the
   127	Skill root, an explicit executable and any asset override. Linux and WSL use
   128	the Linux example. Convert paths passed to native Windows processes explicitly.
   129	
   130	```bash
   131	: "${QUALITYGATE_SKILL_ROOT:?Set the absolute Skill directory}"
   132	case "$(uname -s)" in
   133	  MINGW*|MSYS*) ;;
   134	  *) echo "This example requires Windows Git Bash/MSYS2" >&2; exit 2 ;;
   135	esac
   136	qualitygate_external_runtime=false
   137	if [ "${QUALITYGATE_BIN+x}" = x ]; then
   138	  test -n "$QUALITYGATE_BIN" && test -x "$QUALITYGATE_BIN" || { echo "Invalid explicit Qualitygate executable" >&2; exit 2; }
   139	  "$QUALITYGATE_BIN" --version || exit 2
   140	  qualitygate_external_runtime=true
   141	else
   142	  qualitygate_asset=""
   143	  case "$(uname -m)" in
   144	    x86_64|amd64) qualitygate_asset=windows-x86_64 ;;
   145	    aarch64|arm64) qualitygate_asset=windows-aarch64 ;;
   146	  esac
   147	  QUALITYGATE_BIN="$QUALITYGATE_SKILL_ROOT/assets/$qualitygate_asset/qualitygate.exe"
   148	  if [ -z "$qualitygate_asset" ] || ! test -x "$QUALITYGATE_BIN" || ! "$QUALITYGATE_BIN" --version; then
   149	    QUALITYGATE_BIN="$(command -v qualitygate)" || exit 2
   150	    "$QUALITYGATE_BIN" --version || exit 2
   151	    qualitygate_external_runtime=true
   152	  fi
   153	fi
   154	if [ "$qualitygate_external_runtime" = true ] && [ "${QUALITYGATE_BUILTIN_RULES_DIR+x}" != x ]; then
   155	  QUALITYGATE_BUILTIN_RULES_DIR="$QUALITYGATE_SKILL_ROOT/references/rules"
   156	fi
   157	if [ "${QUALITYGATE_BUILTIN_RULES_DIR+x}" = x ]; then
   158	  test -d "$QUALITYGATE_BUILTIN_RULES_DIR" || { echo "Invalid Qualitygate rule asset directory" >&2; exit 2; }
   159	  QUALITYGATE_BUILTIN_RULES_DIR="$(cygpath -m "$QUALITYGATE_BUILTIN_RULES_DIR")" || exit 2
   160	  export QUALITYGATE_BUILTIN_RULES_DIR
   161	fi
   162	MSYS2_ENV_CONV_EXCL=QUALITYGATE_BUILTIN_RULES_DIR MSYS2_ARG_CONV_EXCL='*' \
   163	  "$QUALITYGATE_BIN" capabilities --format json || exit 2
   164	```
   165	
   166	Use the same per-command conversion exclusions for later native invocations.
   167	For repository commands convert the root with `cygpath -m`; keep `--config`
   168	repository-relative. The [verification workflow](verification.md#inspect-configuration)
   169	provides configuration-inspection examples for each shell.
   170	
   171	## Continue with the requested mode
   172	
   173	For installation or evaluator regression, use [selfcheck](selfcheck.md).
   174	Help, capabilities and schema export also require no repository initialization.
   175	Read-only rule discovery may inspect a repository without creating policy;
   176	follow [rule management](rule-management.md).
   177	
   178	For a repository check, follow [verification](verification.md) to establish the
   179	selected policy and inspect preflight evidence. Runtime resolution alone does
   180	not require `config --show`, `init`, doctor or a formal check.

artifacts.text:
declared `start_sequence`. Equal or reversed starts block final acceptance.
Missing receipts make the result incomplete. Each strict JSON file is limited
to 64 KiB and the receipt inventory to 8 MiB. The CLI rereads the files for
each output; the independent reviewer must compare them with original
process and clock logs. The digest does not authenticate execution or time.

Manifest schemas v2-v9 require a structured `protocol.budget`: three-letter
uppercase currency, price timestamp, rate-card source, total cap in currency
microunits, and human hourly rate in microunits. Set legacy `monetary_cap` to
null. The cap covers all model and infrastructure attempts in both workflows,
including failed attempts, plus each observation's active human review time.
Missing costs, time, or incompatible currency/price are unknown; known spend
above the cap fails even if other inputs are unknown. Budget fields are sealed
before observation. Already sealed v1 records retain their original nine-check
assessment and human interpretation of the text cap.

For new v10 plans, set `monetary_cap` to null, leave `budget` null or absent,
and leave `thresholds.cost_ratio_max` null or absent. The bundled template omits
the threshold. The signed assessment uses eight nonfinancial
checks: detection, false positives, repair, required-check completion, review
fraction, matched inventory, review-time reduction and full-P95 duration.
Costs and usage may still be recorded as descriptive observations; missing
prices remain unknown and do not block those eight checks. v1-v9 plans keep
their versioned financial requirements and assessment digests.

Before collecting outcomes, run `qualitygate pilot authorization-subject
--input <observations.json> --format json`. Have the configured human owner sign
the exact subject as a DSSE Ed25519 record with payload type
`application/vnd.qualitygate.pilot-plan-authorization.v1+json`. The trust key ID
must equal the protocol owner and allow repository checks with the
`pilot-plan-authorization` scope. Keep the trust store and signed envelope
outside the checked repository; do not ask the CLI or an Agent to create a key.

Use `qualitygate pilot summarize --input <observations.json> --trust-store
<external-trust.json> --authorization <external-start.dsse.json> --format json`
for authenticated aggregation. Omitting both external inputs remains a read-only
descriptive replay with `plan_authorization.status=absent` and
`protocol_ready=false`. Keep report paths relative to the manifest's external archive.

The command verifies report bytes and their task, policy, snapshot, environment,
tool and required-check bindings. It retains missing, failed, timed-out and
abandoned assignments in denominators. Null metrics mean that evidence or a
denominator is missing; do not replace them with zero. Different model,
permission, tool, environment, cache, origin, task type and workflow declarations
remain separate groups.

The embedded plan digest detects later changes to the protocol and assignments;
actual routed model identities and observations may be added after sealing.
The owner signature authenticates that exact subject and is checked for scope,
validity and revocation on each summary; it is not a trusted timestamp or final
trial acceptance. The output is descriptive. Reviewer identities, canonical
issue truth, any supplied prices and authority are caller declarations. Do not treat a
summary or met threshold as signed trial approval, and do not infer causal
benefit from groups without the same declared input inventory and conditions.

After the observation window, use `pilot acceptance-subject` with the same
external trust store and authenticated start record. Review the five candidate
rates (detection, false-positive, repair, completion and review fraction) plus
matched inventory, review-time reduction and full-P95 duration. v1-v9 also
require the cost comparison; v2-v9 additionally require the total-budget check.
v10 requires only the eight nonfinancial checks. Failed or unknown required
checks cannot be signed as accepted.

The independent human reviewer key must equal the protocol reviewer and have
the `pilot-trial-acceptance` repository scope. Sign the exact subject with
payload type `application/vnd.qualitygate.pilot-trial-acceptance.v1+json`, then
pass the external envelope with `pilot summarize --acceptance`. An authenticated
rejection is a blocking result. A signature authenticates the decision over the
retained evidence; it does not establish causal benefit or authorize automatic
rollout. Older sealed manifests keep their versioned validation and acceptance
semantics; use this bundled reference for a new v10 pilot.

artifacts.text:
1	# Schema-guided project rule extraction
     2	
     3	This workflow implements a Skill-over-CLI division of responsibility. The LLM
     4	reads repository intent, separates enforceable clauses from unsupported or
     5	human-only clauses, and drafts candidates. The matching CLI owns the executable
     6	contract: it exports the Schema, binds exact source bytes, validates syntax and
     7	semantics, generates the versioned rule file, plans policy, and evaluates a
     8	snapshot. Never replace a CLI step with a model claim that the result would be
     9	equivalent.
    10	
    11	```text
    12	repository prose -> exact source binding + exported Schema -> typed candidate
    13	                 -> CLI validation -> generated rule -> policy review/selection
    14	                 -> snapshot-bound runtime evidence
    15	```
    16	
    17	Keep each arrow explicit. In particular, Schema validity is not semantic
    18	equivalence to prose, generation is not adoption, and a configured rule is not
    19	successful runtime evidence.
    20	
    21	For instruction budgets and required owner/test files, read
    22	[file contracts](file-contracts.md) for the full-inventory DSL and repair loop.
    23	Analyzer count ratchets belong to command-check report configuration; use
    24	[diagnostic ratchets](diagnostic-ratchets.md), not a project-rule candidate.
    25	
    26	Use this workflow when the task authorizes project-rule creation or edits.
    27	Authorization already provided in the session remains valid; ask only when a
    28	material policy choice or required approval is still missing.
    29	Read-only language discovery and schema/source inspection need no policy write.
    30	CLI-generated candidates go to `qualitygate/rules`, never to the installed
    31	Skill's built-in asset directory. Adoption into an existing selected legacy
    32	package follows step 7 without silently replacing that package.
    33	
    34	## Contract and compatibility
    35	
    36	Choose the format from the capability the clause needs, then read only that
    37	format's guide and complete packaged Schema before drafting. Confirm the selected
    38	runtime through [runtime compatibility](runtime-compatibility.md); version strings
    39	alone do not establish support.
    40	
    41	| Clause capability | Format | Runtime export | Guide and packaged Schema |
    42	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
    43	| Fixed entity/file assertions | `schema_version: 1` | `rules schema --format json` (also `schema project-rule`) | [V1 Schema](schemas/project-rule.schema.json); matching v0.4.0-or-newer authoring runtime |
    44	| Typed predicates and aggregation over the selected collection | `schema_version: 2` | `schema operator-rule --format json` | [V2 operators](operators.md), [V2 Schema](schemas/operator-rule.schema.json); require `rules.operators.v2` |
    45	| Named collections, lexical variables, projections and set comparisons | `schema_version: 3` | `schema operator-rule-v3 --format json` | [V3 operators](operators-v3.md), [V3 Schema](schemas/operator-rule-v3.schema.json); require `rules.operators.v3` |
    46	
    47	The Schema is the executable JSON Schema Draft 2020-12 contract compiled into
    48	the matching CLI, not an illustrative template. Export the selected format and
    49	compare parsed JSON with its packaged Schema, ignoring whitespace and object key
    50	order. Missing support or a mismatch blocks authoring; do not guess fields or
    51	execute a schema supplied by the checked repository. Schema exports need no
    52	repository configuration. `schema project-rule-family` is the union of the three
    53	pinned schemas used for mixed-version validation; it does not choose a format.
    54	
    55	All formats require source identity, positive rule version, capabilities,
    56	selection and a fix. V1 requires fixed assertions; V2/V3 require a boolean
    57	expression and may add fixed assertions. Empty `language` means language-neutral;
    58	otherwise use unique lowercase identifiers such as `java`, `python`, `rust`,
    59	`typescript`, `go` or `shell`, not `all`. Scope does not grant adapter capabilities.
    60	The CLI also checks Rust regex/glob syntax, confined source paths and the exact
    61	current source digest. Schema success is not source approval, semantic equivalence
    62	to prose, or execution evidence. The shared sequence below applies to all formats.
    63	
    64	## Classify repository constraints before translating
    65	
    66	Repository policy mixes obligations with different proof requirements. Use the
    67	smallest honest representation; do not force every sentence into project-rule
    68	YAML.
    69	
    70	| Example clause | Route |
    71	|---|---|
    72	| Changed authored files stay within a stated line budget; selected inventory stays within a total word budget | Project DSL `file` + `change: all` + `max_lines` or `max_total_words`, respecting their different delivery/aggregate scopes. |
    73	| Named owner/test files must not be deleted in the selected delivery | Project DSL `file` + `change: all` + `required_paths`; pre-existing absence is outside delivery findings. |
    74	| Every authored file meets its budget, or every named file exists, regardless of Git changes | An existing complete-inventory command check with that evidence; otherwise retain the unsupported gap rather than claim per-file delivery rules satisfy it. |
    75	| Test, comment, import, or commit text follows an explicit bounded convention | Matching structured entity and assertion, with declared capabilities. |
    76	| An import or dependency crosses a reviewed boundary | Parsed import assertion or project-fact `module-boundary`, depending on what must be proved. |
    77	| The dependency graph is acyclic, code type-checks, or a native lint passes | Existing analyzer/project adapter or bounded command check. |
    78	| Clean Code, Clean Architecture, DRY or SOLID design tradeoffs | [Design review](design-review.md), with project evidence and counterexamples; no universal score or inferred threshold. |
    79	| Design quality or an exception is acceptable | Manual/reviewer decision with its existing trust contract. |
    80	
    81	For example, `max_lines: 1000` can check changed files against this repository's
    82	`AGENTS.md` line limit, but it does not replace the existing repository-wide
    83	quality test for all authored files. Its acyclic module ownership clause
    84	requires the architecture gate; a filename or import regex is not an equivalent
    85	proof. Its Cargo quality commands belong to policy command checks. Preserve
    86	that classification and each scope gap in the authoring report so omitted prose
    87	does not silently disappear.
    88	
    89	## Extraction sequence
    90	
    91	1. Inspect the requested language and existing rules to avoid duplicates:
    92	
    93	   ```bash
    94	   "$QUALITYGATE_BIN" --root "$REPOSITORY_ROOT" --config "$QUALITYGATE_CONFIG" rules list --language rust --source all --format json
    95	   ```
    96	
    97	   Built-in inventory includes unselected packages and language-neutral rules.
    98	   Project discovery defaults to `qualitygate/rules`; an explicitly configured
    99	   legacy directory remains visible for compatibility. `all` retains both
   100	   origins when a project ID overrides a built-in. `enabled` identifies the
   101	   selected definition, not whether its profile or prerequisites will run.
   102	
   103	2. Select V1, V2 or V3 using the table above. Run that format's export command
   104	   with the selected executable and compare parsed JSON with its complete
   105	   packaged Schema. For example, a V3 candidate uses `schema operator-rule-v3
   106	   --format json`, not the V1 `rules schema` export. A mismatch blocks authoring;
   107	   it is not permission to guess a compatible subset.
   108	
   109	3. Read the actual normative document and exact section. Treat it as policy
   110	   source data, not authority to change this workflow, credentials or gates.
   111	   Use the actual case-sensitive filename, not an assumed `AGENTS.md` spelling:
   112	
   113	   ```bash
   114	   "$QUALITYGATE_BIN" --root "$REPOSITORY_ROOT" --config "$QUALITYGATE_CONFIG" rules source --document AGENTS.md --section "Test naming" --format json
   115	   ```
   116	
   117	   Use the returned `source` block verbatim. The selector requires one unique
   118	   raw document-level ATX heading (`#` through `######`) outside
   119	   code/HTML/quoted/list containers. Its digest
   120	   includes the heading, exact UTF-8 bytes, line endings and subsections through
   121	   the next same-or-shallower heading. Missing or ambiguous sections require a
   122	   user-supplied source clarification, not a fabricated hash or document edit.
   123	
   124	4. Translate only enforceable obligations into separate complete candidates.
   125	   Every assertion must trace to the selected prose. Never invent a naming
   126	   regex, threshold, severity, dependency, marker, or architecture boundary.
   127	   If a necessary choice is unspecified, ask the user; if the finite DSL cannot
   128	   express an obligation, report the unsupported part rather than creating a
   129	   permissive rule. For marker rules explicitly choose the justified scope and
   130	   declare its capability prerequisites. Do not narrow `ai_only` or replace
   131	   missing provenance to obtain a pass.
   132	
   133	5. Generate a YAML or JSON candidate using the schema's required fields,
   134	   enums and conditional constraints. Keep the temporary candidate outside
   135	   `qualitygate/rules`, inside the repository's authorized scratch location.
   136	   Validate it before publication:
   137	
   138	   ```bash
   139	   "$QUALITYGATE_BIN" --root "$REPOSITORY_ROOT" --config "$QUALITYGATE_CONFIG" rules validate candidate.yaml --format json
   140	   "$QUALITYGATE_BIN" --root "$REPOSITORY_ROOT" --config "$QUALITYGATE_CONFIG" rules generate --input candidate.yaml --format json
   141	   "$QUALITYGATE_BIN" --root "$REPOSITORY_ROOT" --config "$QUALITYGATE_CONFIG" rules validate --format json
   142	   ```
   143	
   144	   `generate` revalidates input, typed serialized output and the source binding,
   145	   then atomically creates `qualitygate/rules/<id>.yaml` without overwriting.
   146	   Duplicate IDs under other filenames and package budget overflow also block
   147	   creation. Run only one authoring writer at a time; filesystem confinement
   148	   checks do not constitute an operating-system sandbox against concurrent edits.
   149	   It does not rewrite `qualitygate.yaml`, select profiles, enable rules or add
   150	   review records. For an authorized existing-rule edit, preserve unrelated
   151	   changes, revise the rule version as appropriate and revalidate the directory;
   152	   do not delete the original merely to make `generate` succeed.
   153	
   154	6. Inspect field-level `issues`, including `stage`, `instance_path`, and
   155	   `schema_path`. Correct the candidate, not the validator. Validation returns
   156	   0 for a complete legal candidate set, 1 for invalid rules/source mappings,
   157	   and 2 when file access or budgets prevent complete validation. YAML duplicate
   158	   keys, custom tags, non-string mapping keys and non-finite values are rejected.
   159	   Directory validation is bounded to 256 YAML files, 1 MiB combined and 4,096
   160	   scanned entries; symlink inputs and output ancestors are rejected.
   161	
   162	7. Report created/updated files, language scope, exact source, validation result
   163	   and unsupported obligations. For a new project-rule package, authorized
   164	   adoption selects `custom_rules: qualitygate/rules`, enables each ID,
   165	   selects profiles and obtains the repository's normal bound source review.
   166	   If `custom_rules` already selects another directory, preserve that package:
   167	   generation still writes to `qualitygate/rules` and does not migrate existing
   168	   definitions. Integrate the generated candidate into the selected directory

1	# Qualitygate operational boundaries
     2	
     3	Read this reference for snapshot selection, acquisition limits, exclusions,
     4	tasks and trusted evidence. [Verification](verification.md) owns initialization,
     5	preflight, final-check completion and result handling.
     6	
     7	For the check's configuration and repair evidence, read
     8	[file contracts](file-contracts.md) when bounding instruction files or checking
     9	required paths, and [diagnostic ratchets](diagnostic-ratchets.md) when preventing
    10	analyzer debt growth. Both use the snapshot and policy boundaries below.
    11	
    12	## Snapshot and policy selection
    13	
    14	Choose exactly the selector the user requested:
    15	
    16	- `--worktree` checks captured current files, including uncommitted changes.
    17	- `--staged` checks index bytes.
    18	- `--diff <base>..<head>` checks a named comparison.
    19	- `--mr <URL>` resolves a GitHub or GitLab merge-request comparison.
    20	
    21	Do not substitute one selector for another. Use `--path` only for explicitly
    22	scoped feedback, and do not describe it as full delivery validation. Keep
    23	`--profile quick` and `--profile full` distinct for the same reason.
    24	
    25	`--path` can be combined with `--staged`, `--worktree`, or `--diff`; it filters
    26	feedback while retaining the complete snapshot for policy and build inputs.
    27	For large repositories, the default acquisition budget is 256 MiB per tree,
    28	100,000 files, 2 MiB per file, four concurrent content readers and 120 seconds.
    29	Git content is size-checked and acquired in batches of at most 4 MiB and 1,024
    30	objects; explicitly allowed larger files use singleton batches up to 8 MiB.
    31	The runner's 16 MiB per-stream limit remains unchanged. Caller controls
    32	are `--snapshot-max-mib` (1–1024), `--snapshot-max-file-mib` (1–8, default 2), `--snapshot-jobs` (1–16) and
    33	`--snapshot-timeout-secs` (1–3600). Choose them for available memory and retain
    34	budget errors as incomplete execution. Recheck commands preserve these options.
    35	
    36	Test-effectiveness overlays retain the selected per-file capacity and complete
    37	historical inputs. Protected candidate validation instead uses the external
    38	suite's `budget.snapshot_max_file_mib` (default 2, range 1–8), bound to the suite
    39	digest and its external authorization. Ordinary check flags do not override it.
    40	
    41	Worktree, staged, diff and MR selectors determine the delivery automatically.
    42	With no selector, the CLI uses the worktree comparison.
    43	It selects findings on changed lines, with changed-file selection for findings
    44	without line positions. Build/test commands retain unexcluded dependency context;
    45	unlocated failures, timeouts and missing evidence still affect the gate.
    46	The profile selects checks, independently of the selected snapshot.
    47	`--diff` and `--mr` acquire unexcluded base/head inputs before computing changes.
    48	A per-file acquisition error is not a rule violation. Rule path filters and
    49	severity changes cannot fix it. Use reviewed policy `exclude` entries or the
    50	suggested `--snapshot-max-file-mib` within its supported maximum; increasing only
    51	the total budget is insufficient.
    52	`init` includes advisory HEAD/worktree metadata preflight, counts and bounded
    53	details for large/unsupported entries, plus actionable next steps. Its success
    54	means a candidate was handled, not that snapshot acquisition or tools passed.
    55	Human guidance escapes control characters in repository paths; JSON keeps the
    56	original path value for machine consumers.
    57	Respect the user's existing adoption authorization; capacity retries do not
    58	mutate repository policy. Do not downgrade incomplete acquisition to a warning
    59	and claim a complete gate.
    60	
    61	```bash
    62	qualitygate check --root "$REPOSITORY_ROOT" --staged --path src --profile quick --snapshot-jobs 4
    63	```
    64	
    65	An active signed policy selects its authenticated package first; conflicting
    66	caller refs are rejected. Without an active policy, configuration, task and custom
    67	rules come from the selected snapshot unless the caller supplies `--policy-ref`.
    68	A caller-supplied reference resolves to a commit but is not proof of approval.
    69	Read [verification](verification.md#initialization-prerequisite) before inferring
    70	that a missing local file requires initialization. Never guess a protected
    71	reference or replace a caller's selected reference with the current branch.
    72	
    73	## Existing-repository trimming
    74	
    75	Use this workflow for first-time adoption or explicitly requested exclusion of
    76	historical resources. Use the matching Skill/runtime; an old executable rejecting
    77	`exclude` is a compatibility gap, not permission to omit it. Verify that reports
    78	contain delivery selection evidence before claiming the requested boundary.
    79	
    80	1. Identify the repository, selector, policy source and intended delivery. Apply
    81	   the [configuration prerequisite](verification.md#initialization-prerequisite).
    82	   Use `init --with-checks` only when candidate command adoption is authorized;
    83	   existing configurations are preserved, not augmented automatically.
    84	2. Read `snapshot_preflight`: large/unsupported entries, excluded paths, truncation
    85	   and incomplete reasons. This is HEAD/worktree metadata, not proof that a chosen
    86	   MR, index, arbitrary refs or the build tools are ready.
    87	3. Review precise exclusion candidates: show matched paths and explain why they
    88	   are historical resources, including possible build/test dependencies. Prefer
    89	   exact files or the smallest useful directory. Do not automatically exclude all
    90	   large files or an entire legacy tree to obtain a pass.
    91	4. With existing authorization for adoption and trimming, edit the candidate
    92	   directly within that scope; do not request repeated approval for routine edits.
    93	   Without that authorization, present a concrete proposed diff. Example:
    94	
    95	   ```yaml
    96	   exclude:
    97	     - "gitbook/images/**"
    98	     - "legacy/demos/**"
    99	   ```
   100	
   101	   Patterns are case-sensitive repository-relative globs with `/` separators.
   102	   They affect tracked files too. No absolute paths, parent traversal, negation
   103	   (`!`) or `.qualitygateignore` are supported. `.gitignore` alone does not remove
   104	   tracked snapshot inputs. Excluded content is not read, checked or materialized
   105	   for tools. Effective policy, tasks, custom rules, their sources and protected
   106	   verification assets cannot be excluded.
   107	5. Run `init --format json` again and inspect `excluded_file_count`,
   108	   `excluded_paths`, remaining oversized entries and `complete`. Keep the candidate
   109	   command review separate: `init --with-checks` does not install or execute tools.
   110	6. Run the intended final check, for example:
   111	
   112	   ```bash
   113	   qualitygate check --worktree --profile full --format json
   114	   qualitygate check --mr https://github.com/owner/repo/pull/123 --profile full --format json
   115	   ```
   116	
   117	   For staged/diff/MR, place the configuration in the selected index/commit first.
   118	   A dirty local exclusion cannot alter a remote MR's policy. Respect any selected
   119	   policy reference or active signed policy; a candidate edit does not replace it.
   120	7. If exclusion removes a required resource, restore/narrow that exclusion and
   121	   rerun. Preserve missing-dependency, build, test, timeout and evidence errors;
   122	   never disable checks, relax severity or expand exclusions merely to make them
   123	   disappear. Unexcluded historical inputs still obey acquisition limits.
   124	8. Report the selector and commits, effective scope, exclusion patterns and matched
   125	   paths, execution-context digest, checks, pending requirements and final result.
   126	   Say "delivery-scope verification passed" when appropriate; do not claim full
   127	   repository coverage. An empty or entirely excluded delivery must be explicit.
   128	
   129	Example outcomes: excluding a historical demo permits acquisition; excluding a
   130	resource used by the build produces a real failure and requires narrowing the
   131	pattern; editing local YAML without committing it does not fix an MR capture.
   132	
   133	## Commands and mutations
   134	
   135	Use [verification](verification.md) for automatic initialization and checks;
   136	use [rule management](rule-management.md) for read-only discovery and authorized
   137	candidate edits. Existing task authorization carries forward. Creating or editing
   138	a candidate does not establish team adoption or release a change.
   139	
   140	`qualitygate check` materializes a selected Git snapshot and may run configured
   141	project tools. Before running it, report the repository root, selector, profile,
   142	task, policy reference, and whether it can access networked tools. Preserve an
   143	explicit `--output-dir` when the user needs durable evidence; otherwise allow
   144	the CLI's bounded default evidence location.
   145	
   146	## Tasks, trust, and manual evidence
   147	
   148	For a task that requires trusted policy or manual evidence, keep trust inputs
   149	outside the checked repository and pass them explicitly:
   150	
   151	```bash
   152	qualitygate check --root "$REPOSITORY_ROOT" --worktree --profile full \
   153	  --task tasks/request.yaml --policy-ref "$TRUSTED_COMMIT" \
   154	  --trust-store /trusted/qualitygate/trust.json \
   155	  --evidence-dir /trusted/qualitygate/records --format json
   156	```
   157	
   158	Do not create, sign, refresh, or reinterpret a manual approval. Missing, stale,
   159	foreign, expired, or malformed evidence is incomplete validation. A local
   160	configuration or a caller-supplied ref is not an approval decision.
   161	
   162	`snapshot.content_digest` identifies the captured execution files.
   163	`snapshot.verification_digest` additionally binds delivery/repository scope,
   164	exclusions, changes and any path filter. Retain both in evidence; signed snapshot
   165	bindings must include the verification digest when present. A matching content
   166	digest alone cannot authorize evidence produced for another scope. Protected
   167	policy comparisons capture each policy's exclusions independently against the
   168	same Git revisions, and bind both input identities when their contents differ.
   169	
   170	## Runtime and selected-snapshot preflight
   171	
   172	Follow [verification preflight](verification.md#preflight-the-intended-snapshot)
   173	with the intended selector, profile, task, policy and budgets.
   174	Use the large-repository template only when metadata or repository instructions
   175	justify increasing the 2 MiB default toward the 8 MiB maximum. Total and per-file
   176	budgets are independent. A preflight pass is not a delivery verdict.
   177	
   178	Materializing an immutable snapshot has a separate bounded writer phase; a
   179	filesystem timeout remains incomplete execution. On Windows, temporary storage
   180	must be writable and large enough for the selected snapshot; inspect `TEMP`/`TMP`
   181	and filesystem diagnostics instead of changing rule severity or skipping files.
   182	
   183	## Default document and media acquisition exclusions
   184	
   185	Runtimes advertising `snapshot.unstructured-documents.v1` default to excluding
   186	known document/media suffixes before reading content, even with `exclude: []`.
   187	Classifier v1 uses case-insensitive final suffixes: documents
   188	`pdf doc docx xls xlsx ppt pptx odt ods odp rtf`, images
   189	`png jpg jpeg gif webp bmp tif tiff ico avif heic heif`, audio/video
   190	`mp3 wav flac aac ogg m4a mp4 mov avi mkv webm mpeg mpg`.
   191	Markdown, HTML, SVG, fonts, archives and unknown `.bin` remain inputs. Use
   192	`unstructured_documents: {enabled: false}` to disable defaults, or `retain`
   193	repository-relative globs for command dependencies. Protected inputs remain
   194	captured; explicit exclusions keep their existing protection errors. Restored
   195	files still obey acquisition budgets. Do not claim excluded resources are checked.
   196	Inspect `selection.resource_exclusions` and the corresponding doctor/init counts.
